module_title: Nobel Prizes - Foundational Facts and Prominent Indian Laureates
introduction: The Nobel Prize is one of the most prestigious international awards, established by the will of Swedish scientist and inventor Alfred Nobel in 1895 (first awarded in 1901). This foundational level covers the basic structure of the awards and the iconic Indian citizens who have brought home this honor.

core_concepts.title: The Six Categories
core_concepts.description: Nobel Prizes are awarded annually in six distinct fields: Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economic Sciences.

core_concepts.title: The First Indian (and Asian) Laureate
core_concepts.description: Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian, and notably the first Asian, to win a Nobel Prize. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his profoundly sensitive poetry collection, 'Gitanjali'.

core_concepts.title: India's First Science Nobel
core_concepts.description: Sir C.V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for his groundbreaking work on the scattering of light, which came to be known as the 'Raman Effect'. National Science Day is celebrated in India on February 28 to mark this discovery.

core_concepts.title: The Peace Laureate
core_concepts.description: Mother Teresa was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for her tireless work in bringing help to suffering humanity through her organization, the Missionaries of Charity.

core_concepts.title: First Indian in Economics
core_concepts.description: Amartya Sen won the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998 for his outstanding contributions to 'Welfare Economics' and social choice theory.

important_entities.name: Alfred Nobel
important_entities.significance: A Swedish chemist and engineer who invented dynamite and left his fortune to establish the Nobel Prizes.

important_entities.name: Kailash Satyarthi
important_entities.significance: Founder of the 'Bachpan Bachao Andolan'. He shared the 2014 Peace Prize with Pakistan's Malala Yousafzai for their struggle for children's rights to education.

important_entities.name: Rabindranath Tagore
important_entities.significance: Not just the first Indian, but the first non-European to win a Nobel Prize.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Origin of the Economics Prize
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common trap! Students often assume all 6 categories started in 1901. The Nobel Prize in Economics was NOT established by Alfred Nobel. It was instituted much later in 1968 by Sweden's central bank and first awarded in 1969.
Though born in Skopje (now North Macedonia), Mother Teresa became a naturalized Indian citizen. Thus, she is officially counted under 'Indian Citizens' who have won the Nobel Prize.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Ravi (Rabindranath - 1913) -> Car (C.V. Raman - 1930) -> Meets (Mother Teresa - 1979) -> A (Amartya Sen - 1998) -> Kite (Kailash Satyarthi - 2014).

exam_strategy_tips: In Tier-1 exams (SSC/Railways), examiners heavily test direct 'Match the Following' questions pairing the Indian laureate with their exact 'Year' and 'Field'. Memorize these five names perfectly.
